title: Investigating the Degradation Mechanism of Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers Using Analytical Electron Microscopy
content: Hydrogen is used in a variety of industrial processes such as ammonia and steel production, petroleum refining, and as fuel to power transportation. Water electrolyzers (WEs) is a promising technology to convert excess electricity from the grid to hydrogen at high efficiency. State-of-the-art WE technology using proton exchange membranes (PEM) have demonstrated both high efficiency and high capacity. The bottleneck for PEMWE, however, is the high cost and lifetime. [1-3] Accelerated stress test (AST) protocols have been developed to evaluate and predict electrolyzer performance and lifetime. Parameters such as dynamic and steady-state load, potential limits, and start-up/shut-down procedures can be designed in AST to investigate the effects of operation on the degradation of PEMWE.
